newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS-Gilt vols shoot up, set to go higher still.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS-Gilt vols shoot up, set to go higher still.

text.p: Implied volatility of gilt options catapulted higher on Wednesday after a shock British interest rate rise, and traders said anxiety ahead of crucial U.S. data would prod it higher still.
"People are buying volatility," said a trader at a continental bank in London.
"I don't think the market thinks it's the end of the whipping around because we've got figures running into the end of the week," he said.
Implied volatility of December out-of-the money options was quoted at around 7.75 percent, up 0.50 percent on the day.
March volatility was quoted at about 7.57 percent versus 7.40 percent in early trade.
The Bank of England earlier raised the minimum lending rate by a quarter-point to 6.0 percent, catching gilt futures and options markets on the hop.
December gilt futures were quoted at 109-22 at 1502 GMT, down 3/32 after dipping to a low of 109-14 after the move.
Analysts said gilts would likely look positively on the rate move as tough anti-inflation medicine after the intitial shock wore off.
Brokers said 112-00 December calls attracted healthy volume. By 1508 GMT, 2,840 lots had changed hands.
The trader at the continental bank said, "All they're doing is trading off the back of volatility as we go up and into the number on Friday," he said.

A broker at French options house in London said investors dived into outright calls and call spreads as the market settled down and before U.S. Q3 GDP data was released. GDP was slightly higher than expected at up 2.2 percent, but final sales were weak and Treasuries moved higher.
Short sterling puts were also active with trade centred on the December 94.00 puts said a broker at a French brokerage in London. More than 3,548 lots were traded by 1508 GMT.
U.S. September payrolls are out on Friday.
